points: 1 Recipe: two stages. First, generative left-to-right LM pre-training (Eq. 1, context window k). Second, discriminative fine-tuning with one added linear+softmax layer W_y on the final block's last-token activation (Eq. 3–4). The LM loss is kept as an auxiliary objective weighted by λ = 0.5 (Eq. 5), claimed to improve generalisation and speed convergence. The only new parameters are W_y and the delimiter embeddings (p. 3–4).

2 Traversal-style input transformations turn structured inputs into one token sequence with start, end and $ delimiter tokens. Entailment: premise $ hypothesis. Similarity: both orderings, representations added element-wise. QA/commonsense: [z; q; $; a_k] per answer, softmax over answers (p. 4).

3 Architecture: 12-layer decoder-only Transformer with masked self-attention, 768-dim states, 12 heads, 3072-dim FFN, GELU, learned position embeddings, BPE with 40,000 merges, tied output embedding (p. 3–4).

4 Pre-training data: BooksCorpus, over 7,000 unpublished books, chosen for long contiguous text over the sentence-shuffled 1B Word Benchmark used by ELMo. Token-level perplexity 18.4, no baseline given (p. 4).

5 Optimisation. Pre-training: Adam, max lr 2.5e-4, 2000-update linear warmup, cosine annealing, 100 epochs, 64 × 512-token minibatches, dropout 0.1, modified L2 w = 0.01. Fine-tuning: lr 6.25e-5, batch 32, about 3 epochs, warmup over 0.2%, classifier dropout 0.1 (p. 4).
6 Withheld: parameter count, compute and training time, corpus size in tokens, seeds/variance/significance tests, dev vs test split for most results.

7 Headline: SOTA on 9 of 12 datasets. NLI (Table 2): MNLI-m 82.1 vs 80.6 (SAN 3x), SNLI 89.9 vs 89.3 (5x ensembles), SciTail 88.3 vs 83.3 (CAFE), QNLI 88.1 vs 82.3 (GenSen), loses RTE 56.0 vs 61.7 (Multi-task BiLSTM+Attn). QA (Table 3): Story Cloze 86.5 vs 77.6, RACE 59.0 vs 53.3 (BiAttention MRU 9x).

8 Table 4 (GLUE tasks): CoLA 45.4 vs 35.0, STS-B 82.0 vs 81.0 (ECNU), QQP 70.3 vs 66.1. Losses: SST-2 91.3 vs 93.2 (Sparse byte mLSTM) and MRPC 82.3 vs 86.0 (TF-KLD). GLUE 72.8 vs 68.9, which does not match the introduction's '5.5%' claim.

9 Ablations (Table 5, unweighted average over 8 GLUE tasks), full model 74.7. Without pre-training: 59.9 ('14.8%' drop, worse on all tasks). Single-layer 2048-unit LSTM: 69.1 ('5.6' drop, wins only MRPC). Without aux LM: 75.0, higher average; the aux LM helps only NLI/QQP, i.e. larger datasets. Table 5 MNLI 81.8 vs Table 2 MNLI-m 82.1 is unexplained.

10 Analysis (Fig. 2, figure only). Each transferred layer helps, up to 9% on MultiNLI. Zero-shot LM heuristics (CoLA, SST-2, RACE, DPRD) rise steadily over pre-training, and the LSTM shows higher variance (p. 7).
